verification.upgrade: The actual canonical SQL preserves synthetic existing free records, shared membership, Auth sessions, and namespaced other-app records; ordinary session insert remains usable and an unregistered marked session is refused.

deployment_gates: Do not run db push against the shared project. Recorded baseline IDs differ from canonical IDs; preserve other-app migration history and reconcile exact source hashes first.

Canonical source files do not prove live schema or managed Auth compatibility. Recheck exact Auth columns, validated nondeferrable single-column user foreign keys, privileges, current Auth version, and ordinary signup/refresh against a disposable clone before deployment.
Auth sessions BEFORE INSERT trigger is always active once applied. Intake disabled does not disable this fence. Changes to managed Auth objects require staged compatibility and rollback review.
Run security/performance advisors against the staged schema; a live advisor before candidate application cannot validate these candidates.
No LOGIN passwords, membership grants, runtime flags, scheduler, retention approval, or production DDL are authorized by this report.
The two-minute marker lifetime and one-day closed-marker purge are implementation candidates, not a published retention SLA.
Review intake is a distinct pending/cancelled receipt, not account deletion completion. Shared Auth erasure and backup/log retention coverage remain incomplete.
managed_auth_caution: Supabase documents that managed non-primary-key columns, indices, constraints and objects can change; a failing Auth trigger may block signup. Test coverage and a TRIGGER privilege alone are not a compatibility guarantee.
